newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 48-hr peso ends weaker on dlr short-cover.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 48-hr peso ends weaker on dlr short-cover.

text.p: Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts reversed earlier gains to close very slightly weaker on Tuesday as local dealers covered short dollar positions ahead of the primary Cetes auction, traders said.
"We had a volatile close as dealers covered dollar shorts to wait and see the outcome of the Cetes auction this evening," one trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso ended 0.2 of a centavo weaker at 7.9930/7.9970 per dollar, while its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.1 of a centavo firmer at 7.9890/7.9930 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed two centavos firmer at 7.9600/7.9650 per dollar.
Traders said they covered short dollar positions in case primary interest rates gained by less than expected at the central bank's primary auction of government securities.

"The peso turned around when dealers saw that rates were not going to gain by as much as the market expected in the morning," another trader said. "I would have seen no problem with a greater increase."
A Reuters survey of eight money market traders in Mexico City showed they expected Banco de Mexico to assign bellwether 28-day rates at 21.61 percent. This would be an increase of 302 basis points.
Nonetheless, foreign exchange traders said they were expected 28-day Cetes rates to gain by 250 basis points.
Banco de Mexico is due to announce primary auction results at 1830 local time/0030 GMT.
Dealers said the peso also weakened in late trade due to a rise in yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds to 6.85 percent, from 6.82 percent in early trade.
